examples.ko: 운전할 때는 핸들을 두 손으로 잡으세요.
examples.en: When driving, hold the steering wheel with both hands.
The steering wheel on this car is too heavy.
I swerved suddenly and avoided an accident.
I hung my bag on the bicycle handlebars.

examples.ko: 핸들 위치를 내 키에 맞게 조절했어요.
examples.en: I adjusted the steering wheel position to my height.
The steering wheel is made of leather, so it is not slippery.

explain: 한국어 '핸들'은 자동차 운전대와 자전거·오토바이의 손잡이 막대를 말해요. 영어 handle처럼 문이나 가방의 손잡이를 '핸들'이라고 하면 어색하고, 그때는 '손잡이'라고 해요. '핸들을 잡다', '핸들을 꺾다'처럼 써요.

phrases.example: 앞에 장애물이 있어서 핸들을 급하게 꺾었어요.
phrases.en: There was an obstacle ahead, so I turned the steering wheel sharply.
phrases.nuance_ko: 운전 중 방향을 갑자기 크게 바꿀 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you suddenly change direction while driving.

phrases.en: To go right, turn the steering wheel slowly.
phrases.nuance_ko: '꺾다'보다 부드럽게 방향을 바꾸는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Feels gentler than 꺾다; a normal turn of the wheel.

phrases.en: The bicycle handlebars were wobbly, so I fixed them.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자동차뿐 아니라 자전거의 손잡이 막대도 '핸들'이라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Besides cars, the handlebars of a bicycle are also called 핸들.

explain_en: Korean '핸들' means a car's steering wheel or the handlebars of a bicycle or motorbike. Calling a door or bag handle a '핸들' is wrong; that is '손잡이'. Use it as '핸들을 잡다' or '핸들을 꺾다'.

t90.ax: I hung my bag on the bicycle handlebars.

examples.en: When the final exams are over, I will go on a trip.
I stayed up all night because of the final exam.
I did well on the final exam, so I feel good.
The final exam covers a much wider range than the midterm.
During final exam period there are no seats in the library.
My English score went up on the final exam.

explain: 학기 가운데 보는 시험은 '중간고사', 학기 끝에 보는 시험은 '기말고사'예요. 줄여서 '기말'이라고도 해요. '시험을 보다'처럼 쓰고 '기말고사를 치르다'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: I take the final exams from tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 가장 많이 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase in daily conversation.

phrases.en: The students are taking their final exams.
phrases.nuance_ko: '보다'보다 조금 더 격식 있는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Slightly more formal than '보다'.

phrases.en: During final exam period, the library is crowded.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시험이 있는 때를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this to refer to the time when exams are held.

explain_en: Common word for the final exam of a term, widely used in speech at schools and universities; near-synonym of 기말시험. A test in the middle of the term is a '중간고사', and one at the end is a '기말고사'. It is also shortened to '기말'. You say '시험을 보다', and also '기말고사를 치르다'.

t90.ax: My English score went up on the final exam.

en: to reinforce; to supplement; to strengthen

examples.en: They reinforced the old bridge with steel bars.
Our team needs to strengthen its defense.

examples.ko: 부족한 부분을 보강하는 자료를 더 찾았어요.
examples.en: I found more material to fill in the weak parts.

examples.ko: 선생님이 결석한 학생을 위해 수업을 보강해 주셨어요.
examples.en: The teacher held a make-up class for the absent students.

examples.ko: 비가 많이 와서 둑을 보강하기로 했어요.
examples.en: It rained a lot, so they decided to reinforce the embankment.

examples.ko: 회사는 새 직원을 뽑아 인력을 보강했어요.
examples.en: The company hired new staff to strengthen its workforce.

explain: '보강하다'는 부족하거나 약한 부분에 더해서 튼튼하게 만들 때 써요. 건물이나 둑은 물론 팀의 선수나 인력, 자료에도 쓸 수 있어요. 학교에서 빠진 수업을 다시 하는 것도 '보강'이라고 해요.

phrases.example: 다리 보강 공사가 한 달 걸려요.
phrases.en: The bridge reinforcement work takes a month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 건물이나 다리를 더 튼튼하게 만드는 공사를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Construction to make a building or bridge stronger.

phrases.en: A new player joined and the team was strengthened.
phrases.nuance_ko: '보강하다'의 피동형으로, 이미 튼튼해진 상태를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The passive form, describing something that has been strengthened.

phrases.example: 비 때문에 빠진 수업은 보강 수업으로 해요.
phrases.en: A class missed because of the rain is made up in a make-up session.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학교에서 빠진 수업을 다시 하는 것을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A class held at school to replace a missed one.

explain_en: To shore up something physical or structural that is weak (담장) 보강하다 means adding to a weak or lacking part to make it stronger. It works for buildings and embankments, and also for a team's players, staff or materials. In school, a make-up class for a missed lesson is also called 보강.

t90.ax: Our team needs to strengthen its defense.

en: to replenish; to supplement; to top up

examples.en: In winter I make up for vitamin D with supplements.
After the presentation, I added the missing content.
Make up for the parts you missed in class with homework.

examples.ko: 부족한 물을 보충하려고 하루에 두 잔씩 더 마셔요.
examples.en: To make up for lacking water, I drink two more glasses a day.

examples.ko: 운동 후에는 수분을 보충하는 것이 좋아요.
examples.en: After exercise, it's good to replenish fluids.

examples.ko: 설명이 부족해서 자료를 하나 더 보충할게요.
examples.en: The explanation was lacking, so I'll add one more document.

explain: 모자란 것을 더해서 채운다는 뜻으로, 영양, 수분, 설명, 수업에 두루 써요. '보완하다'는 약한 부분을 고쳐서 더 낫게 만들 때 쓰고, '보충하다'는 부족한 양이나 내용을 채울 때 써요. '보충 수업'도 자주 써요.

phrases.en: I take a supplementary class during the vacation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모자란 공부를 채우는 수업을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A class that fills in missing study.

phrases.en: After exercise, I replenish fluids with water.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸에 모자란 물을 채울 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for refilling the water the body lacks.

phrases.en: I'll fill in the missing part.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말할 때 내용을 더하겠다고 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in speech when offering to add something.

explain_en: To refill something used up or short in amount (우유, 계란) It means filling in what is lacking, and it is used widely for nutrition, fluids, explanations and lessons. '보완하다' is for fixing a weak point to make something better, while '보충하다' is for filling a shortage in amount or content. '보충 수업' (make-up class) is also common.

t90.ax: After exercise, it's good to replenish fluids.

examples.en: I'm going to the church retreat this weekend.

examples.ko: 신입생 수련회에서 새 친구를 많이 사귀었어요.
examples.en: I made lots of new friends at the freshman retreat.

examples.ko: 수련회 장소는 산속에 있는 조용한 곳이에요.
examples.en: The retreat venue is a quiet place in the mountains.

examples.ko: 수련회 때 밤새 이야기하다가 선생님께 걸렸어요.
examples.en: At the retreat, we talked all night and the teacher caught us.
I went on a two-day, one-night retreat with my club.
I haven't packed the things for the retreat yet.

explain: 학교, 교회, 동아리에서 많이 쓰고, 회사에서는 '워크숍'이라는 말을 더 자주 써요. 대학생들이 놀러 가는 모임은 보통 '엠티'라고 불러요.

phrases.en: I'm going to the school retreat this weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모임에 참가하러 갈 때 '에 가다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with '에 가다' when going to attend the event.

phrases.en: Our club holds a retreat every summer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 행사를 계획하고 진행하는 쪽에서 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used by the side organizing and holding the event.

phrases.en: We had a campfire during the retreat.
phrases.nuance_ko: '때'를 붙여 그 행사 중의 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '때' talks about what happened during the event.

explain_en: A group trip for training or bonding, like a school retreat. It is common for schools, churches and clubs, while companies more often say '워크숍'. A trip where university students go to hang out is usually called '엠티'.

t90.ax: I'm going to the church retreat this weekend.

examples.ko: 수료식에는 가족과 친구들이 와서 함께 사진을 찍었어요.
examples.en: Family and friends came to the completion ceremony, and we took photos together.

examples.ko: 오늘 오후 두 시에 수료식이 있어요.
examples.en: The completion ceremony is at two o'clock this afternoon.

examples.ko: 수료식이 끝나고 다 같이 저녁을 먹었어요.
examples.en: After the ceremony ended, we all had dinner together.

examples.ko: 6개월 과정이 끝나서 다음 주에 수료식을 해요.
examples.en: The six-month course is over, so the ceremony is next week.
I received my certificate at the ceremony and burst into tears.
I was busy and couldn't attend the ceremony, which was a shame.

explain: 학교 전체 과정을 마치는 '졸업식'과 달리 학원, 연수, 교육 과정을 마칠 때 하는 행사예요. 보통 '수료증'을 받아요.

phrases.en: When the training ends, we hold a completion ceremony.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과정이 끝날 때 하는 행사를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the event held when a course ends.

phrases.en: My parents attended the completion ceremony.
phrases.nuance_ko: 행사에 와서 함께한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means being present at the event.

phrases.example: 수료식 날 다 같이 밥을 먹었어요.
phrases.en: On the day of the ceremony, we all ate together.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그날 있었던 일을 말할 때 '날'을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '날' to talk about what happened that day.

explain_en: Marks finishing a course or training program. Unlike '졸업식' (graduation), which marks finishing a whole school program, this is held when you finish a course at an academy or a training program. You usually receive a '수료증' (certificate).

t90.ax: After the ceremony ended, we all had dinner together.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 동네 가게에서 잔심부름을 했어요.
examples.en: When I was little, I ran small errands at a local shop.
New employees start by learning the small errands.

examples.ko: 잔심부름 좀 해 주면 용돈 줄게요.
examples.en: If you run a few small errands for me, I'll give you pocket money.
I was worn out by little errands all day.

examples.ko: 잔심부름이 많아서 정작 제 일은 못 했어요.
examples.en: There were so many odd errands that I couldn't do my own work.
As the youngest, the small office errands are my job.

explain: 우편물 부치기, 커피 사 오기처럼 작고 번거로운 일에 써요. 보통 '잔심부름을 하다/시키다'로 말해요. '잔소리', '잔주름'처럼 '잔'이 붙으면 작고 자질구레하다는 느낌이 있어요.

phrases.en: My dad often has me run little errands.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시키는 사람 입장에서 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said from the point of view of the person giving the errands.

phrases.en: I'm new, so I have a lot of little errands.
phrases.nuance_ko: 직장이나 가게에서 새로 온 사람이 자주 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often said by newcomers at work or in shops.

phrases.example: 새로 온 직원은 먼저 잔심부름을 해요.
phrases.en: A new employee starts by running small errands.
phrases.nuance_ko: '시키다'와 달리 심부름을 하는 사람 입장에서 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Unlike '시키다', this is said from the point of view of the person running the errands.

explain_en: It is used for small, bothersome tasks such as mailing things or buying coffee. It is usually said as '잔심부름을 하다/시키다'. As in '잔소리' and '잔주름', the prefix '잔' gives a feeling of small and minor.

examples.en: Next Friday is the last class of the semester.

examples.ko: 종강 파티는 학교 앞 식당에서 해요.
examples.en: The end-of-semester party is at a restaurant in front of school.
I'm going to start a part-time job after the semester ends.
There are still two weeks left until the end of the semester.
Just before the end of the semester, I said goodbye to my professor.
The exam results came out on the last day of class.

explain: 반대말은 '개강'이에요. 주로 대학에서 쓰고, 초·중·고등학교에서는 '방학식'이나 '종업식'이라고 해요. '종강 파티'처럼 학기가 끝난 기분을 나누는 말과 함께 많이 써요.

phrases.en: I'll hang out with friends on the last day of class.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학기의 마지막 수업 날을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: It points to the last day of class in the semester.

phrases.en: I'm going to travel after the semester ends.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학기가 끝난 뒤의 계획을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it for plans after the semester ends.

phrases.en: The semester is almost over, so I'm studying for exams.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학기가 끝날 때가 다가온다는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means the end of the semester is getting close.
phrases.en_equiv: the end of the semester is near

explain_en: Last class of a semester, school talk (종강 파티) Its opposite is '개강' (start of the semester). It is mostly used for universities; schools below that say '방학식' or '종업식'. It often appears in phrases like '종강 파티' (end-of-semester party).

examples.ko: 시험 시간에 커닝은 절대 하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must never cheat during an exam.

examples.ko: 시험 중에 커닝을 하다가 들켜서 영점을 받았대요.
examples.en: I heard he was caught cheating during the exam and got a zero.
My friend got scolded by the teacher because of cheating.
Cheating is impossible on this test.
I got caught making a cheat sheet.

examples.ko: 우리 반에서 커닝으로 걸린 사람이 없어요.
examples.en: No one in our class has been caught cheating.

explain: 시험에서 몰래 답을 보는 행동만 말하고, 게임이나 연애에서 속이는 것에는 쓰지 않아요. '부정행위'는 공식적인 말이고, 학교에서는 '커닝'이라고 말해요. '커닝 페이퍼'는 몰래 보려고 적어 둔 쪽지예요.

phrases.en: I got caught by the teacher while making a cheat sheet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시험에서 몰래 보려고 적어 둔 쪽지를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A note written to look at secretly during a test.

phrases.en: You must not cheat on a test.
phrases.nuance_ko: '커닝'을 공식적으로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The formal word for cheating.

phrases.en: The teacher changed the seats to prevent cheating.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시험에서 몰래 답 보는 일을 못 하게 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when stopping secret answer-copying in an exam.

explain_en: It only means secretly looking at answers on a test, and is not used for cheating in games or relationships. '부정행위' is the formal term, while at school people say '커닝'. A '커닝 페이퍼' is a cheat sheet written to peek at secretly.

examples.en: I received my report card at school today.

examples.ko: 통지표에 선생님이 좋은 말을 써 주셨어요.
examples.en: The teacher wrote kind words on my report card.
I'm afraid to show my report card to Mom.
The report card comes home before vacation.
My grades on the report card went up from last semester.

examples.ko: 제 통지표를 보고 부모님이 칭찬해 주셨어요.
examples.en: My parents praised me after looking at my report card.

explain: 학교에서 한 학기가 끝날 때 성적과 생활 모습을 적어 집에 보내는 종이예요. 보통 '통지표를 받다/보내다'라고 말해요. 초등학교와 중학교에서 많이 쓰고, 고등학교나 대학교에서는 '성적표'라고 더 자주 해요.

phrases.en: The school sends the report card home.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학교가 집으로 전해 줄 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the school delivers it to the home.

phrases.en: At university, you get a grade report when the term ends.
phrases.nuance_ko: 고등학교나 대학교에서 더 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: More common at high school or university.

phrases.en: My teacher wrote praise on my report card.
phrases.nuance_ko: 통지표에 내용을 쓸 때 '에 적다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '에 적다' to say writing something on it.
phrases.en_equiv: to write on a report card

explain_en: This is the paper a school sends home at the end of a term, listing grades and school life. People usually say '통지표를 받다/보내다'. It is common for elementary and middle school, while for high school and university people more often say '성적표'.

examples.en: The relay race is the most fun at sports day.
Our class took first place in the relay race.
I was the last runner of the relay.
I dropped the baton during the relay.
I watched the Olympic relay on television.
In a relay, teammates must be in sync to be fast.

explain: 계주와 이어달리기는 같은 경기예요. 계주는 한자어이고 이어달리기는 순우리말이에요. 넘겨 주는 막대는 '바통'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: Our class took first place in the relay race.
phrases.nuance_ko: 계주와 같은 뜻의 순우리말이고 말할 때 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A native Korean word with the same meaning, more common in speech.

phrases.en: I was chosen as a relay runner.
phrases.nuance_ko: 계주 경기에 나가는 사람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It names a person who runs in the relay.

phrases.en: I'm running in the relay at this sports day.
phrases.nuance_ko: 경기에 참가한다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say you are taking part in the race.

explain_en: Relay race — team running event, sports day. 계주 and 이어달리기 are the same event. 계주 is a Sino-Korean word and 이어달리기 is a native Korean word. The stick that is passed is called a 바통.

t90.ax: I was the last runner of the relay.

examples.ko: 우리 팀 공격수가 두 골을 넣었어요.
examples.en: Our team's forward scored two goals.
He is a forward famous for his speed.

examples.ko: 공격수가 공을 몰고 골문 앞까지 뛰었어요.
examples.en: The forward dribbled the ball and ran up to the goal.

examples.ko: 새 공격수가 팀에 들어와서 분위기가 좋아요.
examples.en: A new forward joined the team, so the mood is good.

examples.ko: 저는 어릴 때 공격수로 뛰고 싶었어요.
examples.en: When I was little, I wanted to play as a forward.

examples.ko: 공격수는 수비수보다 골을 넣을 기회가 많아요.
examples.en: Forwards have more chances to score than defenders.

explain: 축구 같은 단체 경기에서 공격을 맡은 선수를 말해요. 반대는 '수비수'예요. 축구에서는 '스트라이커'라는 말도 쓰고, 야구에서 공격하는 선수는 '타자'라고 해요.

phrases.en: That player is our team's striker.
phrases.nuance_ko: 축구에서 골을 넣는 일을 맡은 공격수를 가리키는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A word for the attacker whose job is to score goals in soccer.

phrases.en: Our team's forward is very fast.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어느 팀의 공격수인지 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say which team the attacker plays for.

phrases.en: The attackers and defenders run hard together.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반대되는 포지션을 함께 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to name the two opposite positions together.

explain_en: Sports player in the attacking position (축구 공격수), position-based. It means a player in charge of attacking in team games such as soccer. The opposite is '수비수'. In soccer people also say '스트라이커', and in baseball the attacking player is a '타자'.

t90.ax: Our team's forward scored two goals.

examples.en: The child skates through the park on roller skates.

examples.ko: 공사장에서 큰 롤러가 땅을 평평하게 눌러요.
examples.en: At the construction site, a big roller flattens the ground.
Every weekend I go skating with my friend.

examples.ko: 이 롤러는 바퀴가 너무 작아서 불안해요.
examples.en: These skates have such small wheels that they feel unsafe.

examples.ko: 벽은 롤러로 칠하는 게 훨씬 빨라요.
examples.en: Painting a wall with a roller is much faster.
I am more used to a bicycle than to skates.

explain: '롤러'는 롤러스케이트를 줄여 부르기도 하고, 그때는 신을 때 '신다', 탈 때 '타다'를 써요. 공사 장비나 페인트 도구를 말할 때는 '도로 롤러', '페인트 롤러'처럼 앞말을 붙여야 헷갈리지 않아요.

phrases.en: I roller-skate in the park on weekends.
phrases.nuance_ko: 롤러스케이트는 '타다'와 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Roller skates pair with the verb 타다.

phrases.en: I bought new roller skates.
phrases.nuance_ko: '롤러'를 줄이지 않은 원래 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The full, unshortened form of 롤러.

phrases.en: I painted the wall with a paint roller.
phrases.nuance_ko: 도구를 말할 때는 앞에 '페인트'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 페인트 in front when talking about the tool.

explain_en: '롤러' can be short for roller skates, and then you use '신다' (wear) or '타다' (ride). For construction equipment or paint tools, add a word first, like '도로 롤러' or '페인트 롤러', so it is clear.

examples.en: Of all the swimming strokes, the backstroke is the easiest for me.

examples.ko: 배영은 얼굴이 물 밖에 있어서 숨쉬기 쉬워요.
examples.en: In the backstroke your face is out of the water, so it's easy to breathe.
I swam fifty meters using the backstroke.
I'm practicing the backstroke kick.

examples.ko: 배영을 배우고 나서 수영이 더 재미있어졌어요.
examples.en: After learning the backstroke, swimming became more fun.

examples.ko: 배영할 때는 천장을 보면서 팔을 돌려요.
examples.en: When doing the backstroke, you look at the ceiling and rotate your arms.

explain: 자유형, 평영, 접영과 함께 수영 종목 이름이에요. 누워서 천장이나 하늘을 보며 헤엄치는 영법이라 숨쉬기는 편하지만 방향을 보기 어려워요. '배영을 하다'라고 말해요.

phrases.en: I'm learning the backstroke this month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 수영 강습에서 영법을 배운다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you learn a swimming style in a class.

phrases.en: I swam slowly using the backstroke.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 영법으로 수영하는지 말할 때 '~으로'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '~으로' to say which stroke you swim with.

phrases.en: I practiced the backstroke at the pool today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 연습하거나 훈련하는 일을 말할 때 뒤에 '연습'을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '연습' after it when talking about practice or training.

explain_en: Swimming on one's back; Sino-Korean swim term (저는 요즘 일주일에 두 번 수영장에서 배영을 배워요.) It is a swimming stroke name, alongside 자유형, 평영 and 접영. You swim on your back looking at the ceiling or sky, so breathing is easy but it is harder to see where you are going. You say '배영을 하다'.
